reviews.comment: Shes a great professor, especially in office hours. Exams and final = 80%, they are SUPER hw heavy but make sure you know the conceptual stuff too, for MC and TF questions. This class is hard but its a little interesting which makes it bearable. Can't stress enough to know the homeworks inside and out

Explains things super clearly and is always willing to help. DO NOT fall behind in this class as most of it builds upon itself. Tests are easy enough since the homeworks were always harder and served as good practice.
My goat. Her lectures are super clear and she always manages to say the one thing you need to hear that makes it click. She gives examples similar to hw in class

best professor for methods, just attend her lectures and take notes. make sure to actually understand her notes after lecture because she goes really fast. there's a lot of material but she's happy to help and cares that you understand the material. exams are mostly based on homework so just do the homeworks honestly and you should be fine!
Dr. Mio is a good option, 331 has no other options for prof so

As a physics major Dr. Mioduszewski is the best professor I have had thus far. She is extremely reasonable, and she has the best math lectures I have ever had. The homework is out of the textbook, and I would still recommend reading it (especially tensors), but honestly it probably isn't necessary for everyone. A literal gem of a person.

A wonderful professor if you're lucky enough to get her. I was lucky to have her for both PHYS 331 and 332. Tests were not easy, but expectations were very clear and there was never an issue of something being unexpected. So many resources, willing to accommodate, and overall just a wonderful person. Take her if you can!

Dr. Mioduszewski is one of the best profs I've had a TAMU, she does an amazing job in lectures. The exams are challenging but fair and she is easy to get a hold of outside of class. She's in it to make sure you understand the material, not to trick or fail you.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She is very understanding and spends time making sure everyone understands the material. If you email a question she will make sure to review it in class and then do similar problems. Homework is out of the textbook and the lecture notes cover everything.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She was very open to answering questions and helping students better understand concepts.

She is very willing to make time for her students outside of class. Her lectures are well organized and easy to follow, provides homework help, will stop to answer student's questions during lecture. This course is not as horrible as people make it out to be, if you are willing to put in the effort it is doable.

Not an easy class whatsoever. Went to all lectures but never actually paid attention as you're better off doing other homework. Highly recommend getting a season pass at A+ Tutoring and studying the notes from there. Didn't buy the textbook. She does a poor job explaining the concepts and this being a hard class, in general, didn't help.

This class is not quite as bad as everyone says, however it is still absolutely horrible. Mio understands that and tries her best to make the material simple and not waste time on stuff that wont be on the test. She's the only professor that can get you a B without outside help. If you want an A go to A+ or study the textbook like a holy text.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Dr. Mio is a great professor and really cares about her students' learning. She is very good at explaining the material and answering questions students have. The course is difficult meaning the exams are hard and she understands that. So Mio does her best to prepare her students for them. She also gives homework help in class sometimes!

Very patient and overall very good professor! She explains concepts really well and really cares if her students grasp the concepts. She is always available for office hours and gives insightful feedback! Overall, she makes this class very bearable and less scary than it seems. Would definitely recommend!

For sure recommend. She truly tries her best to help students succeed. Her lectures were hit or miss, but that's just the material itself, not her ability to teach. Open to questions and re-clarification. Gives tips on homework, and is extremely well-educated in the field. Go to A+, and you'll be totally fine. Material has real-life applications.
Anyone who rates Dr. Mio bad is just rating the class in general. While it is a difficult class, a good grade is not hard to achieve. Dr. Mio will only make getting that grade easier.
Go to class, read the book, and go to office hours. Dr. Mio is easily the best choice for PHYS-208. She does an awesome job on lectures. 10/10 would recommend.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Best professor for PHYS-208, hands down. Take her and she will help that much more if you're shooting for an A. The class is difficult, but read the book, go to her office hours and actually pay attention in class and you will be fine. 4.0 and Go and A Plus tutoring are a waste. Don't pay for those tutorings. Those students never do well on exams.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Dr. Mio is arguably the best PHYS-208 Prof on campus that teaches University Physics. She provides in depth explanation on the topics of the course and how to solve problems. She cares about you and how you are learning the material. An A in this class is DOABLE. Don't listen to the rumors about PHYS-208 being heard. Dr. Mio will help you get an A!
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: She is a good professor, she explains things quite well. She doesn't like notes being taken on electronic devices. She posts slides from class, and if you have a question, she'll give you a good answer. Also there is a lot of homework, but that is just the class itself.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Mioduszewski was a great prof to take for 208. It's a pretty difficult class but all things considered, she was helpful, understanding, and offered a lot of clarity regarding grades, curves, etc.. Speaks perfect English and is always willing to answer questions both during and outside lecture. Overall, a great prof!

PHYS 208 is a difficult course no matter who your professor is. But, Professor Mioduszewski presents the information very well. Her lectures are clear and she works out example problems in class. She always looks at student comments left on Flip-It (homework due before class) and addresses what students have expressed the most concern about.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Listen here. If you go to aplus tutoring for 208. All the time and do all of the practice problems. You will be fine and even might get an A if you are capable. She is still the best physics teacher probably in the department. Does real life test problems in class and is calm and a good explainer. TEHK HER.

Physics 208 is hard in general. You have to do much more than go to lectures to get a good grade. She is very nice and she does seem to care about if the students understand or not. She will call you out if you use any electronics in her class. She will also get upset if a group of people are joking or talking too loudly.
You will not pass all of your tests unless you are a physics wiz. She isn't a good lecturer, very boring and monotone. MUST go to tutoring to get a good grade.

Physics is so hard in general, but she is a great teacher. Lectures always seem very long, but she makes sure you have an general understanding of what you're doing. Expect a curve. Try your best, and don't get discouraged when you don't make awesome grades.
Phys 218 just sucks in general. No matter who you take, it's hard. Its a common exam, clicker questions happen every class, but she's cool.

PHYS 218 is hard just by being PHYS 218. If you want an A, you'll need to do a lot of the book homework problems. Dr. Mio teaches the University Physics textbook and does a lot of examples and clicker questions in class (so helpful!). She's super sweet and helpful if you go to her office hours. Good teacher, hard course.

She's very helpful, probably one of the best PHYS 218 on campus here at Texas A&M. Her last name is very intimidating but it's not hard to pronounce at all. She has absolutely no accent so it's easy to understand. She has a lot of patience with students and has a passion for physics. I definitely recommend her.

She's a good teacher. She'll help if you ask. She's clear in her lectures. There is a lot of work for this class. Tests are rough. Everyone fails. Lost of homework. And this is probably dependent on your TA but we had a quiz every week in recitation.
